toml:
# GNSS signal availability on the upper-SSV shell: the booklet's global metric, at a size that runs in a second.
#
# The ICG Space Service Volume booklet (UN ST/SPACE/75, 2018) characterises each constellation by the share of time a user
# on a sphere at 36,000 km altitude (the top of the upper SSV) has at least one, and at least four, signals, and by the
# longest outage at the worst point of the sphere. This scenario computes the same metric by the same method (annex B):
# Keplerian orbits of annex C, the main lobe of each transmitter modelled as a constant minimum radiated power inside the
# documented off-boresight angle, a nadir-pointing hemispherical user antenna, Earth blockage by the sphere plus 50 km, and a
# 20 dB-Hz C/N0 threshold for a 0 dBi user antenna.
#
# It is cut down to run quickly: a 162-point grid (the booklet uses 2,562) and 3 days at 10-minute steps (the booklet uses 14
# days at 1 minute). The full-size comparison with the booklet's tables is the pre-registered check in xval/gnss-ssv/.
# MODELLED: the booklet's own results are a simulation, and a main-lobe-only constant-power beam is not a measured pattern.

kind = "gnss-ssv"
name = "Upper SSV shell, 20 dB-Hz (reduced size)"

[constellations]
include = ["gps", "glonass", "galileo", "bds"]
bands = ["l1", "l5"]

[receiver]
cn0_min_dbhz = 20.0

[shell]
altitude_km = 36000.0
antenna = "hemisphere"
grid_levels = 2
duration_min = 4320.0
step_min = 10.0
summary: gnss-ssv shell 36000 km: l1 combined 1+ 99.4% 4+ 73.2%; l5 combined 1+ 100.0% 4+ 99.9%
